title: Controlling Diversity at Inference: Guiding Diffusion Recommender Models with Targeted Category Preferences

problem.claim: Recommendation systems need to control diversity to mitigate bias amplification and filter bubbles, while accommodating diversity targets that may change with user moods or business strategies.

gap.claim: Existing diversity-control methods often lack inference-time flexibility because diversity is determined during training.

contributions.claim: D3Rec is an end-to-end disentangled diffusion recommendation method that controls the accuracy-diversity trade-off during inference.
D3Rec generates recommendations from category preferences, enables inference-time control of those preferences, and adapts to arbitrary targeted category preferences.
D3Rec removes category preferences from user interactions by adding noise in the forward process and reflects desired preferences during reverse-process denoising.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on real-world and synthetic datasets validate D3Rec's effectiveness for controlling diversity at inference.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diversity control is needed to address bias amplification and filter bubbles.
Diversity targets may vary with user moods or business strategies, creating a need for flexible control.
Existing methods generally fix diversity during training and lack easy inference-time modification.
D3Rec separates category preferences through diffusion and incorporates desired preferences during recommendation generation.
Experiments on real-world and synthetic datasets are reported to validate inference-time diversity control.

source_observation.claim: The method exposes category preferences as controllable inputs during inference.

interpretation.claim: Separating a user-facing control variable from the learned generation process can support changing recommendation objectives without retraining.

application.claim: Recommendation systems could offer runtime controls for targeted category exposure or diversity levels.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how arbitrary targeted preferences affect recommendation quality, safety, or user satisfaction.

unknowns: The abstract does not report dataset names, evaluation metrics, quantitative results, or baselines.
The abstract does not describe the scope or operational definition of the accuracy-diversity trade-off.
